In the chapter heading, 孫之旭 is kinship 孫 plus given name 之旭 (Tang Bin's attached grandson), not a man surnamed Sun.
Tang Bin, Sun Zhixu, Lu Longqi, Zhang Boxing
Tang Bin, grandson Zhixu, Lu Longqi, Zhang Boxing
The literal heading likewise misreads 孫 as a surname; 孫之旭 is 'grandson Zhixu.'

Many prefectural and circuit posts stood empty, and the emperor wanted men of both learning and integrity who could turn scholarship to practical use. From the Hanlin Academy he chose Chen Huang, Huang Zhilin, Wang Wujiu, Yang Sisheng, Lan Run, Wang Shunnian, Fan Zhou, Ma Yeeng, Shen Quan, and Bin—ten in all.

Many prefectural and circuit posts stood empty, and the emperor wanted men of both learning and integrity who could turn scholarship to practical use. From the Hanlin Academy he chose Chen Huang, Huang Zhilin, Wang Wujiu, Yang Sisheng, Lan Run, Wang Shunnian, Fan Zhou, Ma Yezeng, Shen Quan, and Bin—ten in all.
馬燁曾 romanizes as Ma Yezeng (燁 yè, 曾 zēng); Yeeng drops 曾 and is not a valid reading.

At the time many prefectural and circuit posts were vacant; the emperor, urgently needing men, sought those combining literary and moral excellence, taking learning as practical statecraft, and selected Hanlin officials, obtaining Chen Huang, Huang Zhilin, Wang Wujiu, Yang Sisheng, Lan Run, Wang Shunnian, Fan Zhou, Ma Yeeng, Shen Quan, and Bin, ten in all.

The literal list repeats the same corrupted romanization of 馬燁曾 as Ma Yeeng instead of Ma Yezeng.
